task_name: Velvet Hour - Social film and story cutdowns
client_brief:
Velvet Hour needs a short film for the next show, a square cut for the feed and the next show poster. The camera sits in the same corner every month and it gives us short silent takes, a few seconds each, with no sound at all, so we are sending five more takes from that corner under the same lamp. Cut the film upright. It is filmed upright and that is where people will watch it.

No narration and no voice over. The words go on screen, set small and quietly, the way we write a listing. The music is the cleared instrumental bed we supply, not a recording of anyone's set, so nothing on these films is anyone's performance audio.

The commission
1. Performance film: 1 named export, 1080 by 1920, 12 to 15 seconds, music from the supplied bed. At least three different takes. The singer stays in frame. The end card bills the next show.
2. Square performance cutdown: 1 named export, 1080 by 1080, 6 to 10 seconds, music from the supplied bed. The singer stays in frame in the square crop.
3. Next show poster: 1 named export, unchanged at 420 by 594 mm, one page. The poster bills all four acts in the lineup's row order and every date is accurate: the first row is the next show and takes the headline with its picture, billing line, date, door time and ticket price, each later act follows with its own date and ticket price, and our moth and lamp mark appears at least once.

Two things matter to us as much as the atmosphere. The act on the end card is next month's act, so bill her as next and do not attribute the footage in the film to her. The billing order, the dates and the prices come from the lineup file and are not ours to reorder or round.

One warning about the framing: the camera clears a pillar, so the singer sits in the left third of the picture and the centre of the frame is a stool and a pair of plain black road cases. A centred crop can be technically correct and still contain no performer, so check the crop rather than trusting it.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. No film in this commission carries speech: the message is carried by on screen text you set, and the music is the cleared bed we supply.
Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for missing coverage.
Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: One night a month, sit down and listen.
brand_identity.sector: Arts, culture and live music (monthly ticketed jazz and folk night)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in the back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island. Tiny: two organisers, ninety seats, one night a month.
brand_identity.about: Velvet Hour is a monthly ticketed jazz and folk night held in the ninety seat back room of a Providence bar. Two sets, no support, one camera in the same corner every month. The night sells intimacy and musicianship to people who read a lineup carefully, so everything we make should feel like a good room rather than a club or a concert hall.

brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, intimate. An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket. Never budget club, never black tie concert hall.

brand_identity.typography: Velvet Hour runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Adobe Caslon Pro Regular 400 at 96 pt on 104 pt leading, tracking minus 5 units on the given name and 120 units on the true small caps surname: the headline act stacked on two lines, given name above surname, so the second line falls quieter than the first. Step 02, subheading, is the same face and stack at 48 pt on 54 pt for support acts, tracking minus 3 units on the given name and 120 units on the small caps surname, with the date line beneath at 24 pt on 30 pt in National 2 Regular. Step 03, body, is National 2 Regular at 11 pt on 16 pt, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters, with the ticket line in National 2 Medium at the same size. Step 04, fine print, is National 2 Regular at 8 pt on 12 pt with tracking of plus 25 units. The film title card carries the same two line stack at 54 px on 64 px. An act name is never set in the sans.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, affectionate, low key. Talks about the room and the players, never hypes. Short sentences, no exclamation, lets the act's face and the music do the work.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our mark, a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type, was made by the designer who set up the night, and the source file went with them when they left. All that survives is the mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box by the door, which is why it has to be rebuilt from that as real artwork. No brand typeface was ever formally chosen, so the type system is open for you to set.
brand_identity.values: Story first, no gimmicks. Clean, coherent, honest to the room. We would rather look like a place people sit and listen than like a night that is trying too hard.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every act name stacks on two lines, given name above surname, with the surname in true Caslon small caps tracked 120 units so the second line falls quieter than the first.

palette_rules.distribution: Back Room Green is the main ground for the poster, the film end card and any solid panel, as on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Lamp Cream is a ground only for a small-print strip, where all type is Warm Ink, as that card's footer. On Back Room Green and over footage, act names, the venue name, billing, door time, price and body are Lamp Cream; the date line may be Ember Amber and the tagline Dust Rose, as on the card. The mark is drawn in flat Lamp Cream on Back Room Green, as painted on velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg. Ember Amber and Dust Rose are accents for hairline rules, the date line and the tagline only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, a panel or an act name.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, any type or the mark, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a photograph: type sits straight on the footage or on a solid Back Room Green card or panel. In the films a card or line may cut or fade in and out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No gold, foil, metallic sheen, glow, drop shadow or other display gimmick on any type, rule, panel or the mark, as the brand's own typography note rules out (“No display gimmicks, no gold foil gestures.”); Ember Amber is always a flat colour. No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules or the mark.
palette_rules.photography: Footage and photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or washed toward the palette. The six takes keep the warm lamp light and the green room as filmed. The act photographs keep natural skin: next_month_act_01.jpg is not pushed grey or orange, and the printed halftone dots in next_month_act_04.jpg are not resampled into a moire. A bar still such as velvet_hour_still_07.jpg keeps natural skin under its warm cast, not taken grey by a whole-frame neutral balance.
